Jordan —

Appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a draft pricing/SLA worksheet (redwood_sla_pricing_v3.xlsx) and a short CSV that shows the "credit formula" examples you can paste into your SOW. High-level answers below — I kept language procurement-friendly and concrete.

Summary (short):
- Aggregation: credits are computed on a 30-day rolling window. Multiple discrete incidents within 24 hours contribute cumulatively to the same rolling window and are additive for credit calculation. Example in the attachment.
- Degraded throughput: we separate "availability" from "performance." Availability (used for credits) is calculated from requests returning 200/accepted within configured SLO latency thresholds. Persistent throughput degradation that causes SLA misses for a request class will count toward availability credits; transient slowdown spikes under 1 minute that do not hit SLOs are excluded.
- Dedicated vs Hosted: the uptime brackets are identical, but response-time SLOs differ by plan: Dedicated customers get committed response windows with a named on-call rota and guaranteed 1-hour initial response for Sev-1; Hosted customers receive a 2-hour initial response for Sev-1 within our premium tier.

Concessions we can make for Acme:
- If you commit to a 12-month $750k ARR contract and provide a single-point PO with net-30, we can: 1) lower the elapsed-credit multiplier by 20% for the first contract year, and 2) include two named escalation contacts in the Dedicated on-call rota at no additional retainer.

I confirmed with Karthik that we can formalize the credit table into a one-page "SLA Exhibit" for your SOW. See the attached.

Next steps:

Jordan —

Quick add from pricing: Naomi captured the commercial levers. Two clarifications we often see in procurement language that will speed approval:

1) Credit calculation example (we put this in sla_credit_formula.csv):
   - Monthly committed uptime = 30 days * 24h = 720 hours. If total downtime (as measured by failed SLO requests) = 3 hours, uptime = (720-3)/720 = 99.583%. Credit = X% based on bracket.

2) Rolling-window vs incident: we will not double-count the same root-cause event across overlapping regions; we aggregate event durations by correlated incident id. Independent incidents are additive. This prevents credit stacking from a single rollout where multiple regions are impacted by the same underlying deploy.

Commercial concession (alternative):
- Instead of lowering the elapsed-credit multiplier, we can offer a flat 10% platform fee credit for the first 90 days if Acme signs a 12-month commit at >= $750k. This is sometimes preferable for customers because it's a fixed-dollar hedge during onboarding.

I'll leave the legal wording to Naomi but happy to join a short call with Procurement if helpful.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Account Strategy
Redwood Inference

Thanks — we can accommodate your asks. Below is a procurement-ready paragraph you can paste into the SOW plus a short definition of measurement. I also added an onboarding credit option to fit net-45. If you confirm, I will create the DocuSign package and route it to your PO contact.

SLA Exhibit paragraph (copy/paste):

"Availability Credits: During each calendar month, Redwood measures service availability for the Services by counting requests that return a successful status code within the configured latency SLO window (as measured by Redwood's API-side telemetry endpoint). Monthly availability = (total SLO-compliant request time / total request time) expressed as a percentage. If monthly availability for the Services falls below 99.9%, Customer will be entitled to a credit as set forth in the following table: 99.9-99.95% = 10% credit; 99.5-99.9% = 30% credit; <99.5% = 50% credit. Credits are applied to the next invoice. Multiple incidents within a 30-day rolling window are additive, except where incidents share a common Redwood incident ID in which case their durations are aggregated and not double-counted.

Measurement definition: Redwood uses API-side telemetry (requests, status codes, and per-request latency percentiles) instrumented at the service edge to calculate SLO adherence. Degraded throughput that results in SLO violations (as measured at the 95th and 99th percentile latency for the affected request class) will be counted toward availability. Transient spikes under 60 seconds that do not violate the configured latency SLO are excluded.

Onboarding credit option (net-45): Because Acme requires net-45, Redwood will apply a one-time onboarding platform credit equal to 5% of first-quarter billed charges, applied on the second invoice, in lieu of the net-30 commercial concession.

We will also include the following operational commitments for Dedicated customers: initial Sev-1 response <= 1 hour (named on-call); initial Sev-1 response for Hosted Premium = <= 2 hours; bridge escalation to Engineering within 2 hours for confirmed platform incidents.

Next steps:
1) Confirm you want the 12-month $750k commit path (and whether you prefer the elapsed-credit multiplier reduction or the 10% fixed onboarding credit) OR accept the net-45 + 5% onboarding credit path.
2) If yes, I will send a DocuSign package (SLA Exhibit + Master Services Agreement redlines) to procure@acme-analytics.com by EOD Aug 23.
